NAME: Top Products per Category
DESC:
The merchandising team wants, for each product category, the best-selling products by net units sold. Returns are recorded as sales with a negative quantity. The ingestion job sometimes loads the same sale twice.

Implement solve so that it returns the top n ranks of products in each category.

Input

sales_df

column type description
sale_id string identifies a sale; rows with the same sale_id are identical copies
category string free text with inconsistent case and spaces; may be null
product_id string may be null
quantity int negative for a return; may be null
sale_date string format yyyy-MM-dd (not needed for this task)

n is a positive integer.

Rules

  1. Each sale_id is counted once.
  2. category is normalized by trimming spaces and converting to lowercase.
  3. Rows whose normalized category is null or empty, whose product_id is null, or whose quantity is null are ignored.
  4. total_units of a product in a category is the sum of the quantities of its sales in that category (returns included). The same product_id in two categories is ranked separately in each category.
  5. Products whose total_units is 0 or negative are excluded.
  6. Within each category, products are ranked by total_units descending. Products with the same total_units share the same rank, and ranks have no gaps: totals 9, 9, 7 get ranks 1, 1, 2.
  7. Return every product whose rank is less than or equal to n.

Output

A DataFrame with exactly these columns, in this order:

column type
category string
product_id string
total_units long
product_rank integer

Rows are sorted by category ascending, then product_rank ascending, then product_id ascending.

Example

n = 2

sales_df

sale_id category product_id quantity sale_date
S1 "electronics" P1 5 2024-03-01
S2 " Electronics" P2 3 2024-03-01
S3 "electronics" P3 5 2024-03-02
S4 "ELECTRONICS" P4 2 2024-03-02
S5 "electronics" P2 -1 2024-03-03
S6 "books" B1 4 2024-03-01
S6 "books" B1 4 2024-03-01
S7 "books" B2 null 2024-03-02
S8 "books" B3 -2 2024-03-03
S9 null P9 10 2024-03-03

Expected output

category product_id total_units product_rank
books B1 4 1
electronics P1 5 1
electronics P3 5 1
electronics P2 2 2
electronics P4 2 2

Function signature

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame

def solve(sales_df: DataFrame, n: int) -> DataFrame:
    ...

Constraints

  • Use the PySpark DataFrame API. Do not convert to pandas and do not call collect() or toPandas() inside solve.
  • sales_df has up to 10^7 rows; 1 <= n <= 100.
  • The returned DataFrame may be empty; its columns and types must still match the specification.

SOLUTION:
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame, Window
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(sales_df: DataFrame, n: int) -> DataFrame:
    # 1. Doublons de ré-ingestion : même sale_id = même vente, comptée une fois.
    #    Puis normalisation de la catégorie et rejet des lignes inutilisables.
    category = F.lower(F.trim(F.col("category")))
    clean = (
        sales_df
        .dropDuplicates(["sale_id"])
        .withColumn("category", category)
        .filter(
            F.col("category").isNotNull() & (F.col("category") != "")
            & F.col("product_id").isNotNull()
            & F.col("quantity").isNotNull()
        )
    )

    # 2. Unités nettes par (catégorie, produit), retours inclus ; total <= 0 exclu AVANT le classement.
    totals = (
        clean.groupBy("category", "product_id")
        .agg(F.sum("quantity").alias("total_units"))
        .filter(F.col("total_units") > 0)
    )

    # 3. dense_rank : ex aequo au même rang, pas de trou.
    w = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy(F.col("total_units").desc())
    ranked = (
        totals
        .withColumn("product_rank", F.dense_rank().over(w))
        .filter(F.col("product_rank") <= n)
    )

    return (
        ranked
        .select("category", "product_id", "total_units", "product_rank")
        .orderBy("category", "product_rank", "product_id")
    )
